## 1

We want to find the estimation for this integral using standard normal distribution. $\theta$ can be view as $\theta = \int_1^{\infty} g(x)f(x)dx$ where $g(x) = x^2$ and $f(x) = \frac{1}{\sqrt{2 \pi}} e^{-x^2/2}$, $1 < x <$ $\infty$. 

What I'm going to do is sample from standard normal distribution, and then insert these samples X to g(x). Therefore, we can get $E[g(X) I(X > 1)]$ which is the estimation for this integral.


```{r q1}
set.seed(1024)
n <- 10000
X <- rnorm(n) 
g <- X^2 * (X > 1)

theta_hat <- cumsum(g) / seq_len(n)

f <- function(x) (x^2 / sqrt(2 * pi)) * exp(- x^2 / 2)
theta <- integrate(f, lower = 1, upper = Inf)

plot(theta_hat, type = "l", xlab = "sample size")
abline(h = theta$value, col = "red")

```

## 2
```{r q2_importance sampling}
set.seed(1024)
n <- 10000
x <- rnorm(n)

g <- function(x) {
  x^2 / sqrt(2 * pi) * exp(-x^2 / 2) * (x > 1)
}
fg <- g(x) / (1 / sqrt(2 * pi) * exp(-x^2 / 2))
theta_hat <- mean(fg)

fg_cum <- cumsum(fg) / seq_len(n)

f <- function(x) (x^2 / sqrt(2 * pi)) * exp(- x^2 / 2)
theta <- integrate(f, lower = 1, upper = Inf)

plot(fg_cum, type = "l", xlab = "sample size")
abline(h = theta$value, col = "red")

```


```{r}
set.seed(1024)
n <- 10000
x <- rnorm(n, mean = 2, sd = 1)
w <- dnorm(x) / dnorm(x, 2, 1)
h <- x^2 * (x > 1)
theta_hat <- cumsum(h * w) / cumsum(w)

f <- function(x) (x^2 / sqrt(2 * pi)) * exp(- x^2 / 2)
theta <- integrate(f, lower = 1, upper = Inf)

plot(theta_hat, type = "l", xlab = "sample size")
abline(h = theta$value, col = "red")


```

## 3
Let $y = 1/x$, then $dy = \frac{-1}{x^2} dx$. We can therefore get $\theta = \int_1^0 \frac{-x^4}{\sqrt{2 \pi}} e^{-x^2 / 2} dy = \int_0^1 \frac{1}{y^4 \sqrt{2 \pi}} e^{-1 / 2y^2} dy$. 

Then we can simply generate samples U from $Uniform(0,1)$ and insert it into $\frac{1}{y^4 \sqrt{2 \pi}}$ $e^{-1 / 2y^2}$. After that, we can get the estimation for $\theta$.

```{r q3}
set.seed(1024)
n <- 10000
u <- runif(n)
Y <- 1 / (u^4 * sqrt(2 * pi)) * exp(-1 / (2 * u^2))

theta_hat <- cumsum(Y) / seq_len(n)

f <- function(x) (x^2 / sqrt(2 * pi)) * exp(- x^2 / 2)
theta <- integrate(f, lower = 1, upper = Inf)

plot(theta_hat, type = "l", xlab = "sample size")
abline(h = theta$value, col = "red")


```
## 4
Two control variates I use are $f_1(u) = u$ and $f_2(u) = u(1 - u)$, where $U \sim Uniform(0, 1)$. Based on the result of question 3, we let our target to be$g(x) = \frac{1}{x^4 \sqrt{2 \pi}} e^{-1/2x^2}$. 

```{r q4}
set.seed(1024)
n <- 10000
u <- runif(n)
g <- 1 / (u^4 * sqrt(2 * pi)) * exp(-1 / (2 *u^2))
f1 <- u
f2 <- u * (1 - u)

L <- lm(g ~ f1 + f2)
c1 <- -L$coefficients[2]
c2 <- -L$coefficients[3]
T_cv <- g + c1 * (f1 - 0.5) + c2 * (f2 - 1/6)

theta_hat <- cumsum(T_cv) / seq_len(n)

f <- function(x) (x^2 / sqrt(2 * pi)) * exp(- x^2 / 2)
theta <- integrate(f, lower = 1, upper = Inf)

plot(theta_hat, type = "l", xlab = "sample size")
abline(h = theta$value, col = "red")

```

## 5


```{r}
set.seed(1024)
M <- 10000
n <- 10
r <- M / n
N <- 1000
T2 <- numeric(n)
estimates <- numeric(N)


g <- function(x) {
  1 / (x^4 * sqrt(2 * pi)) * exp(-1 /(2 * x^2))
}

f <- function(x) (x^2 / sqrt(2 * pi)) * exp(- x^2 / 2)
theta <- integrate(f, lower = 1, upper = Inf)$value 

n <- c(1, 2, 5, 10, 50, 100, 500, 1000)
result <- matrix(0, 8, 3, dimnames = list(n, c("mean", "sd", "bias")))

for(i in 1:length(n)) {
  k <- n[i]
  T2 <- numeric(k)
  for(j in 1:N) {
    for(p in 1:k) {
      T2[p] <- mean(g(runif(M/k, (p-1)/k, p/k))) 
      }
    estimates[j] <- mean(T2)
  }
  result[i, 1] <- mean(estimates)
  result[i, 2] <- sd(estimates)
  result[i, 3] <- mean(estimates) - theta
}
result

```

## 5
```{r}
set.seed(1024)
n <- 10000
Y <- function(x, t) x^2 * dnorm(x) / dnorm(x, t, 1) * (x > 1)
t_grid <- seq(-10, 10, by = 1)
result <- matrix(0, length(t_grid), 2, dimnames = list(t_grid, c("mean", "sd")))

for(i in 1:length(t_grid)) {
  t_val <- t_grid[i]
  x <- rnorm(n, t_val, 1)
  T1 <- Y(x, t_val) 
  result[i, 1] <- mean(T1)
  result[i, 2] <- sd(T1) / sqrt(n)
}
result


```
